chunks: "Do not eat the slaughtered animal of the Jew, the Christian, the Magian, and everyone who opposes the religion, except when you hear him mention the Name of Allah over it. And in the Book of Ali عليه السلام: "The Magian does not slaughter, nor the Christian, nor the Christians of the Arabs, the sacrificial animals." And he said: "You may eat his slaughtered animal if he mentions the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.اسْمَ اللَّهِ: the Name of Allah, whose mention over the animal is treated as legally significant
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian, mentioned here in the ruling on slaughter
key_terms.الْأَضَاحِيَّ: the sacrificial animals offered as udhiyah
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيِّ: a Magian or Zoroastrian, mentioned here in the ruling on slaughter
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew, mentioned here in the ruling on slaughter
key_terms.ذَبِيحَةَ: the slaughtered animal whose permissibility is being discussed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the slaughtered animal of a Jew, Christian, or Magian in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the permissibility of eating slaughtered animals prepared by non-Muslims and others who oppose the religion. It emphasizes the mention of the Name of Allah as a determining condition and also cites a ruling preserved in the Book of Ali عليه السلام regarding sacrificial slaughter.
